title: Small cocartesian presentations over a small base
statement: Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, small simplicial sets and essential smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], quasicategories and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cocartesian fibrations and fibers of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $S$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory and let $p:E\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration with $E$ fitting in $\mathcal U'$. Suppose that for every vertex $s\in S$ the fiber $E_s$ is equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory. Then there exist a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $E_0$, a cocartesian fibration $p_0:E_0\to S$, and a functor $F:E_0\to E$ with $pF=p_0$, such that $F$ is a functor equivalence, every fiber functor $F_s:(E_0)_s\to E_s$ is a functor equivalence, and $F$ preserves and reflects cocartesian edges. Empty bases and empty fibers are allowed.

source.place: Remark 3.3.2.3, property (*′) on printed p. 211 (PDF p. 229), cocartesian dual, with Theorem 3.2.0.1 and section 3.3.2 (classification). General small-model consequence over a small base, not a verbatim monoidal assertion. Read online; archival HTT copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Choose an auxiliary universe $\mathcal U''$ containing $\mathcal U'$. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] with object universe $\mathcal U'$: its total-space smallness assumption is now satisfied by $E$, and $S$ is also $\mathcal U'$-small. We obtain a classifying coherent functor $\chi:S\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U'}$ with $\chi(s)\simeq E_s$ at each vertex. Each $\chi(s)$ is therefore equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory: compose this equivalence with the assumed small model of $E_s$. No local smallness assumption on the given simplicial set $E$ is needed.

source.place: Remark 3.3.2.3: classify in the enlarged universe first

proof.text: Let $J:\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U'}$ be the fully faithful universe inclusion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening-universe-change]. Let $H$ be its full replete essential image. All vertices of $\chi$ belong to $H$ by step 1, so every simplex of $\chi$ belongs to $H$ by the definition of full subcategory in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; hence $\chi$ factors as $\chi_H:S\to H$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to $J$, in the auxiliary universe containing both category objects. It gives a coherent quasi-inverse $K:H\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ to the restriction of $J$. Put $\psi=K\chi_H$. Whiskering the given counit $J K\simeq1_H$ with $\chi_H$ gives a coherent natural equivalence $J\psi\simeq\chi$. Thus this is a single coherent small-valued diagram, including its higher simplices, rather than unrelated choices of models of the fibers.

source.place: Remark 3.3.2.3, (*) and (*′): essential-image factorization of the classifying diagram

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] with object universe $\mathcal U$ to $\psi$. This is legitimate because its indexing quasicategory is the given $\mathcal U$-small $S$. Choose a simplicial cocartesian fibration $p_0:E_0\to S$ in $\operatorname{coCart}_{\mathcal U}(S)$ with $\operatorname{St}^{\mathcal U}_S(p_0)\simeq\psi$. In particular $E_0$ is $\mathcal U$-small, not merely $\mathcal U'$-small. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening-universe-change], its classifying diagram in $\mathcal U'$ is equivalent to $J\psi$, hence to $\chi$ by step 2. Applying a quasi-inverse of the larger straightening equivalence and its inverse-equivalence data gives an equivalence from $I_S(p_0)$ to $p$ in $\operatorname{coCart}_{\mathcal U'}(S)$. This uses essential surjectivity only at the small-universe application and then compares two objects in the same larger cocartesian category.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.0.1 and Remark 3.3.2.1: small-universe unstraightening and comparison in the larger universe

proof.text: Use the cocartesian dual of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] in $\mathcal U'$ to represent the equivalence of step 3 by a cocartesian-edge-preserving simplicial map $F:E_0\to E$ strictly over $S$, with an edge-preserving inverse $G:E\to E_0$ up to coherent natural equivalences over $S$. The theorem identifies the relative sharp mapping complexes with cores of the categories of such maps, so these inverse data are actual maps and paths over $S$. Thus $pF=p_0$. Forgetting the condition of being over $S$ leaves a quasi-inverse and two coherent natural equivalences, so $F$ is a functor equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restrict the same maps and equivalences degreewise to $s$: because their base maps are constant in the homotopy parameter, they give $F_s,G_s$ with both inverse equivalences. Every $F_s$ is consequently a functor equivalence. These restrictions also make sense for an empty fiber.

source.place: Definition 3.3.2.2: equivalence over the fixed base; marked-model realization and restriction to fibers

proof.text: Preservation of cocartesian edges is part of the map $F$ in step 4. To verify reflection, let $e:x\to y$ be an edge of $E_0$ and suppose $F(e)$ is $p$-cocartesian. For each vertex $z\in E_0$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] in $E$ with test object $Fz$. Its square is a homotopy pullback. The square in $E_0$ for $e,z$ maps to this square, with identity maps on the two base mapping spaces and equivalences on the two total mapping spaces: [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] supplies the latter because $F$ is a functor equivalence. In the path-space models of the two pullbacks, [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] makes the comparison of the other three corners an equivalence. Two-out-of-three applied to the comparison from the upper left corner therefore makes the $E_0$ square a homotopy pullback. The mapping criterion in $E_0$ proves that $e$ is $p_0$-cocartesian. This tests every required $z$, without requiring a choice of representatives of all objects of $E$. If $S$ is empty, the map $E\to S$ forces $E$ empty degreewise, and $E_0=\varnothing$ satisfies the conclusion directly; none of the other steps requires nonempty fibers.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, cocartesian dual: reflection of the mapping-space universal property; empty-base check

proof_origin.place: Explicit universe descent and relative equivalence argument following Theorem 3.2.0.1 and Remarks 3.3.2.1–3.3.2.3, with reflection from the dual of Proposition 2.4.4.3. Read online; no archival HTT copy is present. The universe-compatibility comparison is isolated as a statement-only node.

lean.note: Small and large simplicial sets are represented in the containing universe max (u + 1) v. The recorded Presentability.IsSmall predicate expresses actual u-smallness of the base and output total simplicial set, distinct from essential smallness of the input fibers. The fiber comparison is the canonical pullback.map of the strict over-base comparison.
